stem_bark.text: The bark of Polyalthia suberosa is corky, ridged (deeply fissured) and brown-greyish coloured. The young branchlets are rufous and tomentose.
stem_bark.text_html:

seed.text: The seeds of Polyalthia suberosa are globose and smooth. There is one seed per drupe.
seed.text_html: The seeds of Polyalthia suberosa are globose and smooth. There is one seed per drupe.

fruit.text: The fruit of Polyalthia suberosa is an aggregate of drupes. The fruitlets are subglobose and 6-7 mm across. The fruits are violet-black when ripe with a 4-5 mm long and slender stalk.
fruit.text_html: The fruit of Polyalthia suberosa is an aggregate of drupes. The fruitlets are subglobose and 6-7 mm across. The fruits are violet-black when ripe with a 4-5 mm long and slender stalk.

images.caption: Polyalthia suberosa fruits (ripe, right and unripe, left)
Polyalthia suberosa not yet ripe fruits

flower.text: The flowers of Polyalthia suberosa are solitary and axillary. The pedicel is slender and about 1-1.5 cm long. The calyx is composed of 3 ovate-triangular and spreading sepals. They are 2 mm long and 2 mm wide. The sepals are light green, pubescent outside and glabrous inside. The corolla is composed of 6 (3+3) yellowish green petals. The outer petals are ovate-triangular (acute apex), shorter than inner petals (3x2 mm), outside pubescent and inside glabrous. The inner petals are oblong with an acute apex, erect and curved, 6-8 mm long and 3 mm wide. The androecium is composed of numerous, 1 mm long stamens. The pistil is composed of a short and oblong style and a triangular and flat stigma . There are 1 or 2 ovules per carpel. The carpels are stalked and pubescent.
flower.text_html:
The flowers of Polyalthia suberosa are solitary and axillary. The pedicel is slender and about 1-1.5 cm long.
The calyx is composed of 3 ovate-triangular and spreading sepals. They are 2 mm long and 2 mm wide. The sepals are light green, pubescent outside and glabrous inside.
The corolla is composed of 6 (3+3) yellowish green petals. The outer petals are ovate-triangular (acute apex), shorter than inner petals (3x2 mm), outside pubescent and inside glabrous. The inner petals are oblong with an acute apex, erect and curved, 6-8 mm long and 3 mm wide.
The androecium is composed of numerous, 1 mm long stamens.
The pistil is composed of a short and oblong style and a triangular and flat stigma. There are 1 or 2 ovules per carpel. The carpels are stalked and pubescent.

leaf.text: The leaves of Polyalthia suberosa grow alternately on the stem (distichous). The leaves have a 0.5 cm long petiole. The leaf is simple, bright green coloured above and paler beneath. The leaf is coriaceous, shiny and glabrous on both sides (some minute hairs on the margins and on the midrib beneath). The leaf of Polyalthia suberosa is 8-13 cm long and 3-4 cm wide. The shape is elliptic, the apex is acute to acuminate (sometimes obtuse), the base is cuneate and the margins are entire. The venation of the leaf is reticulate with a prominent midrib.

distribution.text: Polyalthia suberosa is an understorey species of evergreen forests of the coasts from the plains to 1000 m on the hills. Indo-Malesia biogeographical region.

leaf.text: The leaves of Syzygium caryophyllatum are simple, growing in an opposite and decussate arrangement. The petiole is less than 1cm long, canaliculate and glabrous. There are many lateral nerves close, slender and prominent looped at the margin.

stem_bark.text: The culms of Cymbopogon martini are growing from 1.5 m up to 3 m long. They arise from a short, stout, woody rootstock. The culm-nodes flush with the internodes, the lower nodes are often swollen.

flower.text: The flowers of Cymbopogon martini are growing in erect false panicles. The false panicles are linear-oblong, up to 30 cm long. The spatheoles are narrowly elliptic or lanceshaped, 2 to 4 cm long. The spatheoles are green in colour becoming orange or red at maturity. The racemes are 1.5 to 2 cm long, the lowermost pedicle is swollen and barrel-shaped. The internodes and flower-stalks are densely fringed with hairs along the margins and are sparsely hairy on the back. The sessile spikelets are elliptic-oblong or oblong in shape and about 4.5 mm in size. The lower glume is flat on the back in the upper half and with a deep V-shaped groove in the lower. The keels are winged above. The upper lemma is deeply bifid, with an awn of 1.2 to 1.8 cm long.

The trunk is often short and crooked. The stems are long and flexible. The young branches are densely covered with short soft hairs.

flower.text: The flowers of Hibiscus tiliaceus are 3 to 5 cm wide. It is covered in yellow anthers with a terminal, red, five-parted style.

flower.text: The flowers of Rauvolfia tetraphylla are grouped in axillary or terminal few-flowered cymes . The calyx-tube is cup-shaped, 5-lobed and 2 mm long and 2.5 mm wide. The calyx is light green and finely pubescent. The corolla-tube is 3.5 mm long and 2 mm wide. The corolla is 5-lobed. The corolla-lobes are ovate, 1.5 mm long and 1 mm wide. The corolla is white and light green-coloured and pubescent without. The androecium is composed of 5 stamens. The filaments are about 1.5 mm long. The style is filiform, 2 mm long with a capitate stigma . The flowers are fragrant.

The flowers of Rauvolfia tetraphylla are grouped in axillary or terminal few-flowered cymes.
The calyx-tube is cup-shaped, 5-lobed and 2 mm long and 2.5 mm wide. The calyx is light green and finely pubescent.
The corolla-tube is 3.5 mm long and 2 mm wide. The corolla is 5-lobed. The corolla-lobes are ovate, 1.5 mm long and 1 mm wide. The corolla is white and light green-coloured and pubescent without.
The androecium is composed of 5 stamens. The filaments are about 1.5 mm long.
The style is filiform, 2 mm long with a capitate stigma.
The flowers are fragrant.

leaf.text: The leaves of Rauvolfia tetraphylla grow in fours on the stem. The leaf is simple, bright green-coloured above and paler beneath. The leaf is chartaceous and tomentose on both sides. The leaves have a 6-7 mm long petiole . The leaf of Rauvolfia tetraphylla is 5-10 cm long and 2-4 cm wide. The shape of the blade is elliptic, the apex is acute or obtuse, the base is rounded and the margins are entire. The venation of the leaf is reticulate with a prominent midrib.

habit.text: Rauvolfia tetraphylla is a thornless, much-branched and deciduous shrub growing up to 2-3 m high.
habit.text_html: Rauvolfia tetraphylla is a thornless, much-branched and deciduous shrub growing up to 2-3 m high.

distribution.text: Rauvolfia tetraphylla is found in "wet to dry thickets, often in second growth or in waste ground or old fields, usually at elevations below 500 metres". ( Useful Tropical Plants Database, Ken Fern, 2014 (http://tropical.theferns.info) ). Rauvolfia tetraphylla is native to tropical America but the species is now widely cultivated and naturalised throughout the tropics.

reproduction_dispersal.text: Rauvolfia tetraphylla is bisexual (each flower of each individual has both male and female structures). Rauvolfia tetraphylla is pollinated by a wide variety of insects. The seeds of Rauvolfia tetraphylla are mainly dispersed by frugivorous birds and mammals.

reforestation.text: Rauvolfia tetraphylla can be planted in the sun or half shade. It is drought resistant and it will grow in a wide variety of situations and soils but all soils need to be free draining. The species is propagated by seeds or by cuttings. 24 hours of soaking in water accelerates the germination process.
